shortDescription: WALTHAM, Mass., Oct. 18, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Spyre Therapeutics, Inc. children: , a clinical-stage biotechnology company committed to developing next-generation therapies that elevate the standard in immunology by delivering more complete disease control, greater durability, and a simpler treatment experience for patients, today announced presentations at United European Gastroenterology Week (UEGW) 2026 in Barcelona. The presentations include the first scientific congress presentation of clinical data across all three of Spyre’s IBD antibodies—SPY001 (anti-α4β7), SPY002 (anti-TL1A), and SPY003 (anti-IL-23)—which are now being tested as monotherapies and pairwise combinations in the SKYLINE study, as well as new preclinical data demonstrating additive efficacy of these complementary mechanisms.

“Despite significant advances in the treatment of IBD, many patients still do not achieve or maintain the level of disease control we would like to see, underscoring the need for new approaches that can deliver deeper and more durable responses,” said Silvio Danese, M.D., Ph.D., Professor of Gastroenterology at Vita-Salute San Raffaele University and Head of the Gastroenterology and Endoscopy Unit at IRCCS San Raffaele Hospital in Milan, and Chair of the SKYLINE trial Steering Committee. “We believe that advanced combination therapy provides a strong probability of enhanced efficacy compared to today’s monotherapies, and Spyre’s approach of combining optimized versions of antibodies against proven targets represents one of the most promising pipelines in the field. With clinical proof-of-concept now demonstrated across SPY001, SPY002 and SPY003, we are increasingly excited to see the combination results next year with the potential to raise the therapeutic ceiling for patients with IBD.”
The poster and presentation will be available for viewing during UEGW, and details are as follows:
: Efficacy and Safety of Half-Life Extended Antibodies SPY001, SPY002, and SPY003 for Induction Treatment of Moderately to Severely Active Ulcerative Colitis
Silvio Danese, M.D., Ph.D., San Raffaele Hospital
: Anti-α4β7 integrin, anti-TL1A, and anti-IL-23 are efficacious in TNBS-induced colitis using humanized mice, and combinations further improve efficacy
Full session details can be accessed via the UEGW program.

Spyre Therapeutics is a clinical-stage biotechnology company committed to developing next-generation therapies that elevate the standard in immunology by delivering more complete disease control, greater durability, and a simpler treatment experience for patients. Spyre's pipeline includes investigational extended half-life antibodies targeting α4β7, TL1A, IL-23, and IL-17A/F as well as rational combination programs.
